options.A: Fungi colonize the bladder wall and obstruct the normal flow of urine
options.B: Bacteria enter the systemic circulation and settle permanently in the heart valves
options.C: Pathogens ascend from the cervix through the uterus into the fallopian tubes and pelvic cavity
options.D: Viruses alter bone marrow production, leading to severe immunological suppression

explanation: PID happens when bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix, causing widespread inflammation in the upper reproductive organs.

question: What is your very first step when a patient has dry chemical powder spilled all over their skin?

options.A: Wrap the area tightly with a clean sterile bandage
options.B: Scrub the affected skin vigorously with a stiff brush
options.C: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly over the powder
options.D: Brush away the loose powder before using water

explanation: Always brush dry powder off first! Adding water right away to some chemicals can trigger a fiery reaction or make the chemical burn worse.

question: What type of lining tissue covers the inside of the respiratory tract?

options.A: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium
options.B: Simple cuboidal glandular epithelium
options.C: Transitional muscular epithelium
options.D: Stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium

explanation: Even though the medical name sounds like a tongue-twister, you'll see it everywhere in nursing! This special tissue has tiny hair-like cilia that sweep dirt and germs right out of your airways.

question: A ward manager in a public hospital faces severe supply shortages and staff burnout. What is the best way to handle this leadership challenge?

options.A: Waiting passively for central government authorities to fix all facility problems
options.B: Strictly punishing staff members whenever minor supply miscounts occur
options.C: Using adaptive authority to build consensus, mentor staff, and solve problems creatively
options.D: Ignoring hospital protocols entirely and letting junior nurses run the ward

explanation: When resources are tight, great leaders don't just punish—they lean on teamwork, mentor each other, and find creative local solutions to keep caring for patients.

question: Which nurse behavior is most likely to drive a teenager away from a health clinic permanently?

options.A: Empathetic counseling
options.B: Moralizing and scolding
options.C: Active listening
options.D: Warm greeting

explanation: Teens are super sensitive to criticism. If they expect to be judged or lectured, they'll avoid getting the care they need.

question: Which device is best suited for automatically sending daily blood glucose readings to a nurse?

options.A: A remote patient monitoring device
options.B: An ordinary paper nursing notepad
options.C: A standard mercury sphygmomanometer
options.D: A hospital bedside surgical tray

explanation: Remote monitoring tools are designed to track and transmit vital health metrics directly to healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h2)

question: How does a nurse leader best support junior nursing staff on the ward?

options.A: By doing all their clinical paperwork so they never write notes
options.B: By punishing them publicly whenever a minor mistake occurs
options.C: By keeping them isolated from doctors and therapists
options.D: By empowering them and fostering an encouraging work environment

explanation: Spot on! Great leaders lift others up, creating a safe space to ask questions and learn without fear.

question: How is quality improvement (QI) different from traditional medical research?

options.A: Quality improvement focuses entirely on blaming staff, while research focuses on patients
options.B: Research uses simple bedside charts, while quality improvement requires complex laboratories
options.C: Quality improvement tracks workflow changes, while research seeks to prove broad theories
options.D: Research has no clinical value, while quality improvement replaces clinical judgment

explanation: Think of it this way: research tries to discover brand-new general knowledge for textbooks, while QI tests quick fixes right there on your local hospital ward!

question: What should you check or do first when a patient is brought in with a suspected poisoning?

options.A: Drawing blood for toxicology screening
options.B: Identifying the specific poison
options.C: Administering activated charcoal immediately
options.D: Stabilizing the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: Great nursing rule to keep in mind! ABC comes before anything else in an emergency. We have to make sure our patient is breathing and has a steady heartbeat before we worry about testing or finding out what they swallowed.

question: How do vocational and peer support programs help a patient newly released on parole?

options.A: They completely replace the need for antipsychotic medications.
options.B: They rebuild daily routines, confidence, and social connections.
options.C: They guarantee that the patient will never feel stressed again.
options.D: They allow the legal system to close the patient's case file forever.

explanation: You got it! Healing goes beyond just stopping symptoms; patients need help rebuilding their confidence, daily habits, and friendships.

question: A gifted child gets extremely upset over loud noises or small unfairness in class. What explains this?

options.A: Oppositional defiant tendencies
options.B: Sensory and emotional overexcitabilities
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Typical delayed impulse control

explanation: Gifted kids often feel the world with extra intensity! Their nervous systems pick up on sounds, sights, and feelings much more strongly than others. Well done!

question: How do smart beds help keep vulnerable hospital patients safe?

options.A: They automatically administer pain medication when turning
options.B: They replace the need for physical therapists on surgical wards
options.C: Built-in scales eliminate the need to chart daily fluid intake
options.D: Sensors alert staff when an unassisted patient tries to stand up

explanation: Brilliant! Smart bed exit alarms give you a quick heads-up so you can rush over and prevent a nasty fall.

question: Which body tissue is mainly responsible for movement and pumping blood?

options.A: Nervous tissue
options.B: Muscle tissue
options.C: Connective tissue
options.D: Epithelial tissue

explanation: Muscle tissue is built to contract and shorten, making it the powerhouse behind every movement you make.

question: Which activity is a classic example of primary prevention?

options.A: Giving routine childhood immunizations
options.B: Treating complications of advanced diabetes
options.C: Performing a blood pressure screening clinic
options.D: Providing physical therapy after a stroke

explanation: Vaccines protect healthy people from contracting a specific disease in the first place, which defines primary prevention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h2)

question: What crucial warning must you give a patient who takes daily anti-seizure medication?

options.A: Only take the pills on days when you feel a headache coming on
options.B: Never stop taking the medication suddenly without consulting your doctor
options.C: Stop the medication immediately if you go one week without a seizure
options.D: Take a double dose whenever you feel stressed or tired

explanation: Spot on! Quitting anti-seizure meds abruptly can trigger dangerous rebound seizures or status epilepticus. Always taper safely with a doctor's guidance.

question: What is the difference between anonymity and confidentiality?

options.A: Anonymity means no one can link data to a name; confidentiality keeps known identities secret
options.B: Anonymity is optional in nursing research; confidentiality is strictly mandatory
options.C: Anonymity applies only to secondary data; confidentiality applies to primary data
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms in clinical research studies

explanation: Anonymity means nobody (not even the researcher) knows whose data is whose. Confidentiality means you know who they are, but you keep their identity locked away safe.

question: When is medication reconciliation most critical for a patient?

options.A: During every routine morning bath
options.B: Only when the patient is discharged home
options.C: During transitions of care between settings
options.D: Right before a surgical incision is closed

explanation: Medication reconciliation is vital whenever a patient moves between different healthcare settings or levels of care, as this is when errors happen most. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient eats a snack with 10g of carbs, 5g of protein, and 4g of fat. What is their total calorie intake?

options.A: 60 kcal
options.B: 96 kcal
options.C: 76 kcal
options.D: 19 kcal

explanation: Let's break it down: Carbs (10 x 4 = 40), Protein (5 x 4 = 20), Fat (4 x 9 = 36). Add them up (40 + 20 + 36) to get 96 total calories. You're doing great with math!

question: Why are babies born to teenage mothers more likely to have a low birth weight?

options.A: Adolescent mothers usually consume excessive dietary supplements
options.B: Placental function is always enhanced in teenage pregnancies
options.C: The young mother's body is still competing for nutrients with the fetus
options.D: Fetal growth stops completely during the third trimester

explanation: Since the young mother is still growing herself, her body shares vital nutrients with the baby, often leaving both short on what they need.

question: A baby is born at 36 weeks with clear fluid, but has weak muscle tone and is gasping for air. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Move the baby to the warmer for initial steps
options.B: Immediately start chest compressions and epinephrine
options.C: Administer rescue breaths using a bag-valve-mask
options.D: Leave the baby with the mother for skin-to-skin care

explanation: Poor tone and gasping mean the baby needs extra help right away. Take them to the radiant warmer to clear their airway and help them breathe.

question: What does it mean when a microorganism is simply 'colonizing' a patient?

options.A: The microorganism lives on or in the body without causing tissue damage
options.B: The pathogen has invaded deep tissues and caused severe organ failure
options.C: The bacteria are spreading rapidly through the bloodstream to the brain
options.D: The immune system has completely destroyed all traces of the microbe

explanation: Colonization means the germ is hanging out and multiplying on the skin or mucous membranes without making the person actively sick.

question: What does cultural competence mainly ask of a home health nurse?

options.A: Convincing the family to adopt modern medical lifestyles
options.B: Speaking multiple local languages fluently
options.C: Accepting and respecting diverse family lifestyles and beliefs without judgment
options.D: Refusing to care for patients with unfamiliar cultural practices

explanation: You got it! You don't have to share every belief, but respecting a family's unique culture is key to building true healing relationships.

question: Why is it best to use both quantitative and qualitative methods during your community assessment?

options.A: It is required by law to spend extra ministry funding
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to speak to villagers directly
options.C: It combines measurable statistics with deep human context
options.D: It ensures that no written reports need to be created

explanation: Numbers give you the stats (how many people are sick), but talking to people gives you the story (why they are sick and what stops them from getting help). You need both!

question: Why do cells in a tissue live surrounded by an extracellular matrix?

options.A: To hold the cells together and help them share a common function
options.B: To generate electrical impulses for the nervous system automatically
options.C: To prevent any fluid from ever moving between the cells
options.D: To completely isolate each cell from its neighbors for protection

explanation: The extracellular matrix acts like mortar in a brick wall, holding the cells together so they can work as a solid team.

question: What is the very first priority when handling a suspected child abuse case?

options.A: Reuniting the child with extended family members immediately
options.B: Ensuring the physical safety and medical stabilization of the child
options.C: Conducting a lengthy family therapy session at the bedside
options.D: Waiting for legal court orders before treating physical wounds

explanation: Safety first! Always treat urgent medical needs and get the child away from immediate danger before anything else.

question: Which organ is the main player in the 'first-pass effect' for oral drugs?

options.A: The kidneys
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The liver
options.D: The stomach

explanation: You guessed it—the liver! Blood from the gut goes straight to the liver via the portal vein, where enzymes process and break down a portion of the drug before it hits the rest of the body.

question: Why must nurse managers be careful with how much time is spent in meetings?

options.A: Because clinical staff prefer attending meetings over working on the ward
options.B: Because hospital accreditation bodies require a specific number of meeting hours
options.C: Because meetings are the only way to evaluate nurse performance
options.D: Because poorly run meetings pull staff away from patient care without adding value

explanation: Every minute in a meeting is time away from the bedside. Good managers make sure meetings are truly worth it!

question: What is the main difference between casual drug use and addiction?

options.A: Taking a prescribed cough syrup for a cold
options.B: Compulsive drug seeking despite harmful physical or social results
options.C: Using traditional herbs for malaria treatment
options.D: Drinking a single glass of wine at a family wedding

explanation: Addiction takes over a person's life, creating an unstoppable urge to find and use the drug even when it causes serious harm.

question: Which type of medication is given to treat intestinal worm infections?

options.A: Antihypertensives
options.B: Anthelmintics
options.C: Antivirals
options.D: Antifungals

explanation: Think 'anti' (against) and 'helmintic' (worms)! Anthelmintics are the specific drugs nurses administer to clear out parasitic worms.

question: What is it called when a baby's head is simply too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

options.A: Uterine inversion
options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: Don't let the big words scare you: 'cephalic' means head, 'pelvic' means pelvis, and 'disproportion' means a size mismatch between the two!

question: What test is always needed to give a 100% definitive diagnosis of cancer?

options.A: Tissue biopsy
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Ultrasound scan

explanation: Scans and blood tests give us great clues, but looking at a tiny tissue sample under a microscope is what confirms cancer for sure.

question: How can a nurse tell the difference between normal pregnancy breathlessness and a serious lung issue?

options.A: Serious lung problems disappear completely as soon as the patient drinks water
options.B: Normal dyspnoea lacks warning signs like chest pain, coughing blood, or low oxygen levels
options.C: Normal dyspnoea causes blue lips and severe finger clubbing
options.D: Normal dyspnoea only occurs when the patient is lying flat on her back

explanation: Ordinary shortness of breath feels safe and stable, but red flags like chest pain or low oxygen mean we must investigate right away.

question: Why is interprofessional collaboration essential for patient outcomes?

options.A: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without nurse interference
options.B: It eliminates the need for written medical records
options.C: It combines different professional skills to prevent gaps in patient care
options.D: It allows nurses to avoid talking directly to patients

explanation: Working together across disciplines ensures holistic, error-free care by utilizing each professional's unique expertise. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h7)

question: How do cultural and religious beliefs typically impact family planning efforts in certain communities?

options.A: They force every household to adopt strict two-child limits.
options.B: They guarantee immediate funding for health facilities.
options.C: They automatically eliminate all maternal mortality rates.
options.D: They can create suspicion toward birth control and promote large families.

explanation: In some communities, large families are traditionally tied to prestige and wealth. This can make people suspicious of modern contraceptives until we gently educate them.

question: Under normal circumstances, how often should you check cervical dilation during active labour?

options.A: Once every 24 hours
options.B: Every 30 minutes
options.C: Every 4 hours
options.D: Every 15 seconds

explanation: Checking every 4 hours gives you a clear picture of how labour is advancing while keeping the risk of infection low.

question: A young patient is worried that getting a contraceptive implant will make her permanently barren. How should you reassure her?

options.A: Confirm her fear and advise her to avoid all modern methods
options.B: Suggest she use ineffective traditional herbs instead
options.C: Ignore her concern and insert the device without discussion
options.D: Explain that fertility returns quickly once the implant is removed

explanation: You nailed it! Explaining that these methods are fully reversible helps calm her fears and builds strong trust.

question: How does the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) protect the public from unsafe practice?

options.A: By setting scopes of practice, licensing nurses, and enforcing discipline
options.B: By providing free housing for newly graduated nurses
options.C: By hiring domestic staff for community health centers
options.D: By managing the financial budgets of all private hospitals

explanation: Spot on! By licensing only qualified practitioners and keeping an eye on professional conduct, the NMCN ensures patients are always in safe hands.

question: Why do patients on blood thinners still rely on their body's natural healing to clear old clots?

options.A: Natural defenses are permanently shut down by the drugs
options.B: Medications destroy platelets before they reach the clot
options.C: Anticoagulants lack the ability to break down established fibrin
options.D: Anticoagulants only slow down the heart rate

explanation: Anticoagulants prevent new trouble, but breaking down existing clots is a job for the body's own natural cleaning system! Great job reviewing this.

question: What is the main difference between a refugee and an internally displaced person (IDP)?

options.A: Refugees receive permanent housing immediately.
options.B: Internally displaced persons have lost their citizenship.
options.C: Refugees have crossed an international border.
options.D: Internally displaced persons live outside their home country.

explanation: You've got this! Think of it simply: refugees cross international borders to find safety, while IDPs are forced to move but stay inside their own country. Both need our care as nurses!

question: What is the first blood collection step when performing a standard GTT?

options.A: Drawing blood immediately after drinking the glucose drink
options.B: Drawing a baseline fasting blood sample
options.C: Waiting two hours before taking any blood sample
options.D: Checking urine glucose before touching the patient

explanation: A fasting blood sample must always be collected first to establish the patient's baseline glucose level before giving the drink. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h4)

question: Which feature is a must-have for a true experimental research design?

options.A: Observation of natural behaviors
options.B: Random assignment of participants
options.C: Qualitative interview transcripts
options.D: Retrospective chart reviews

explanation: For an experiment to be truly 'true,' you need to randomly assign people to groups, actively change an independent variable, and have a control group to compare them against.

question: Which layer of the hydatid cyst makes the fluid and new parasite cells?

options.A: Epicyst
options.B: Ectocyst
options.C: Endocyst
options.D: Pericyst

explanation: The inner layer, called the endocyst, is the active part that produces fluid and new cyst parts.

question: What is a very common immediate complication right after FGM is performed?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Hemorrhage and severe pain
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Cutting heavily supplied blood vessels in the genital area without anesthesia causes severe bleeding and intense pain right away.

question: What should a nurse researcher do if a routine check reveals a dangerous new health issue in a participant?

options.A: Wait until the entire multi-year study is finished before telling anyone
options.B: Inform the participant immediately and help them access proper medical care
options.C: Delete the test result from the computer so nobody else can see it
options.D: Ignore the finding because research data should never interfere with treatment

explanation: You've got it! Patient safety and our duty of care as nurses always come first, way ahead of research data goals.

question: After giving a patient a strong painkiller through an IV, what is your most important follow-up duty?

options.A: Check back within a short window to evaluate pain relief and watch for breathing problems
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately since pain management is complete
options.C: Document that the patient is cured of all chronic illnesses
options.D: Wait until the next morning to ask if the pain went away

explanation: Powerful painkillers need close monitoring. You want to make sure the pain is actually easing up, and that the patient's breathing stays safe and steady.

question: What is the main reason a researcher tries to control variables in a study?

options.A: To ensure patients never experience any side effects
options.B: To make the research process as fast as possible
options.C: To isolate the specific effect of the intervention being tested
options.D: To hide unwanted data from the final report

explanation: Brilliant! Controlling variables helps you say for sure: 'Yes, this specific drug or nursing action is what made the patient better.'

question: As a nurse writing notes for a domestic violence survivor, how should you document physical injuries?

options.A: Avoid writing down statements made by the patient about the assault
options.B: Discard the documentation if the police are not immediately called
options.C: Include personal opinions about the partner's character in the notes
options.D: Use objective descriptions of the injuries and obtain patient consent

explanation: Correct! Always stick to clear, factual descriptions of what you see and get the patient's okay to protect their rights.

question: What is the right move when a study throws a totally unexpected result your way?

options.A: Throw away the entire dataset and start the study over
options.B: Discuss them honestly and suggest potential reasons for the outcome
options.C: Blame the participants for failing to follow instructions properly
options.D: Pretend the unexpected data points do not exist in the report

explanation: You've got this! Honesty is everything in research. Surprising results often teach us the most valuable lessons.

question: What is the main job of nutrition in the human body?

options.A: Eliminating the need for physical exercise
options.B: Providing energy and building blocks for repair
options.C: Increasing overall body temperature constantly
options.D: Preventing all known genetic disorders

explanation: Spot on! Food gives our bodies the fuel we need to move around, stay alive, and heal when we get hurt.

question: What is an important nursing intervention during a home visit to a patient with severe dementia?

options.A: Changing the patient's daily medication schedule constantly
options.B: Encouraging the patient to live completely alone without any help
options.C: Assessing the home environment for safety and fall hazards
options.D: Arguing with the patient to prove what year it currently is

explanation: Safety assessments are vital for cognitive-impaired clients who may wander, misplace items, or encounter household dangers. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h7)

question: What is the most common and versatile suturing technique used for simple emergency lacerations?

options.A: Retention bridge stitch
options.B: Simple interrupted suture
options.C: Subcuticular continuous stitch
options.D: Continuous running lock

explanation: Simple interrupted stitches are quick to place and provide reliable closure where each stitch stands alone. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does urine actually travel from the kidneys down to the bladder?

options.A: Cilia beating along the mucosal lining
options.B: Cardiac output and arterial blood pressure
options.C: Passive gravity pulling fluid downward
options.D: Peristaltic smooth muscle contractions

explanation: Fantastic! Even if you are lying flat on your bed, those smooth muscle squeezes keep urine moving nicely.

question: What natural body process helps the uterus contract and shrink back down after delivery?

options.A: Oxytocin release stimulated by breastfeeding
options.B: Complete bed rest for the first week
options.C: Increased production of progesterone
options.D: Immediate resumption of heavy exercise

explanation: Amazing! When the baby suckles, the brain releases oxytocin. This hormone causes those strong, helpful uterine cramps that shrink the uterus and stop bleeding.

question: What tool is commonly used in skilled care settings to assess and track resident health status?

options.A: Minimum Data Set (MDS)
options.B: Pediatric growth chart
options.C: Surgical safety checklist
options.D: Emergency room triage scale

explanation: The Minimum Data Set (MDS) is a standard assessment tool used in long-term care facilities to evaluate how a resident is doing.

question: According to the Swiss Cheese Model, what usually causes patient harm?

options.A: A combination of multiple small system failures
options.B: Unavoidable natural deterioration of medical tools
options.C: Sudden refusal of treatment by the patient's family
options.D: Intentional sabotage by a single disgruntled worker

explanation: Errors usually happen when several safety checks fail all at the same time, letting a mistake reach the patient.

question: What is the exact infectious stage of the parasite that actually enters the human body?

options.A: Miracidia
options.B: Metacercariae
options.C: Cercariae
options.D: Adult fluke

explanation: You nailed it! Humans catch the infection by swallowing encysted metacercariae hiding in raw or poorly cooked freshwater crabs and crayfish.

question: What is the main role of the basal ganglia in motor control?

options.A: Generating electrical impulses inside individual muscle fibers
options.B: Selecting desired movements while suppressing unwanted ones
options.C: Carrying sensory signals up the spinal cord to the brain
options.D: Sensing pain and temperature from the hands and feet

explanation: The basal ganglia act as a filter that allows intended movements to happen smoothly while blocking competing, unwanted muscle actions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h3)

question: How has the primary role of the nurse changed from early historical times to today?

options.A: It evolved from informal domestic charity to an autonomous regulated profession
options.B: It changed from independent medical diagnosis to unpaid domestic work
options.C: It shifted from hospital administration to strictly religious duties
options.D: It transformed from a male-only military role to a purely clerical office job

explanation: Think about how far we've come! Modern nursing requires formal education, licensing, and independent critical thinking, rather than just basic home caregiving. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following belongs to the epidemiological component of a health profile?

options.A: Prevalence of malaria and malnutrition rates
options.B: Total number of children enrolled in primary school
options.C: Condition of roads leading to the primary health center
options.D: Average monthly income of market women

explanation: Epidemiology looks at disease patterns, illness rates, and health conditions affecting the population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h3)

question: An endometrioma happens when which of the following occurs?

options.A: Ovarian surface cells multiply and produce thick mucus
options.B: The corpus luteum traps blood inside its cavity after ovulation
options.C: Uterine lining tissue grows on the outside of the ovary
options.D: An unruptured egg follicle swells excessively with clear fluid

explanation: Think of endometriomas (often called chocolate cysts!) as happening when tissue similar to the lining of the uterus decides to grow outside on the ovaries.

question: What is the main chemical messenger the endocrine system uses to send signals around the body?

options.A: Electrolytes
options.B: Hormones
options.C: Neurotransmitters
options.D: Plasma proteins

explanation: Think of hormones as the body's internal mail system! Endocrine glands release them straight into the bloodstream to tell different organs what to do.

question: Roughly how many extra daily calories does a breastfeeding mother need?

options.A: 1000 to 1200 kilocalories
options.B: Zero extra calories are needed
options.C: 450 to 500 kilocalories
options.D: 100 to 150 kilocalories

explanation: Making breast milk takes a lot of body power! Mums actually need even more extra energy daily while breastfeeding than they did while pregnant.

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their birth control method?

options.A: Forgetting clinic locations
options.B: Traveling out of the country
options.C: Experiencing side effects
options.D: Changing religious beliefs

explanation: When clients face physical or emotional side effects that they don't know how to handle, they usually stop using the method.

question: Why are nurses considered frontline workers in infection surveillance?

options.A: They spend the most time observing patients at the bedside
options.B: They design the computer software used for hospital records
options.C: They are the only staff allowed to write public health laws
options.D: They fund all the laboratory testing in the facility

explanation: Bedside presence allows nurses to spot early signs of infection before anyone else. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h5)

question: What percentage of the annual national budget did the Abuja Declaration recommend for health spending in African countries?

options.A: Exactly 5 percent
options.B: At least 15 percent
options.C: Up to 50 percent
options.D: Not more than 2 percent

explanation: The famous Abuja Declaration set a benchmark of 15 percent for government investment in health. Memorize this one—it's a classic exam favorite!

question: A nurse notices that a medication dose for postpartum bleeding is written unclearly on the chart. What is the safest immediate action?

options.A: Clarify the order with the prescribing doctor before giving the drug
options.B: Guess the correct dosage based on the patient's general appearance
options.C: Skip the medication dose entirely without telling anyone
options.D: Administer the medication quickly to avoid wasting valuable time

explanation: You nailed it! Never guess when administering drugs. Verifying unclear orders protects both your license and your patient from harm.

question: How do poor internet and lack of journal access affect local nursing research?

options.A: They prevent nurses from wearing their uniforms to work
options.B: They force patients to travel abroad for medical treatments
options.C: They increase the number of medication errors in the wards
options.D: They make thorough literature reviews and data analysis very difficult

explanation: Spot on. Without good internet access, checking what other researchers around the world have discovered becomes a massive struggle.

question: What is the primary purpose of data organization in nursing research?

options.A: To publish findings without peer review
options.B: To eliminate the need for statistical testing
options.C: To increase the total number of study participants
options.D: To structure raw information so it can be analyzed

explanation: Organizing raw data transforms messy notes and numbers into a structured format that allows researchers to look for patterns and run accurate analysis. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h1)

question: In advanced breast cancer, what causes that dimpled 'peau d'orange' (orange peel) skin texture?

options.A: Blockage of the dermal lymphatic vessels by cancer cells
options.B: An allergic reaction to topical herbal ointments
options.C: Bacterial infection of the superficial sweat glands
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to dry skin flaking

explanation: When cancer cells block the tiny lymph channels in the skin, fluid backs up and creates that bumpy, orange-peel look.

question: What does the basal metabolic rate measure?

options.A: Total calories burned during heavy physical exercise
options.B: Extra calories burned due to cold weather exposure
options.C: Energy used specifically to digest a large meal
options.D: Minimum calories needed for basic life functions at rest

explanation: BMR is the baseline energy required by the body to sustain vital organs while completely at rest. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h2)

question: What happens if a nurse manager ignores a small workplace disagreement?

options.A: It will automatically resolve itself over time.
options.B: It can grow into a major crisis that threatens patient safety.
options.C: It will improve overall staff productivity.
options.D: It will make doctors respect nurses more.

explanation: Unresolved issues fester and ruin teamwork, which can sadly put patient care in danger. Good to know!

question: How is explanatory research different from just watching patients in the ward?

options.A: Explanatory research requires no data collection from actual human subjects
options.B: Explanatory research looks for the underlying reasons behind an event, not just the facts
options.C: Observation is done by doctors while explanatory research is strictly for nursing students
options.D: Observation uses numerical data while explanatory research only uses spoken stories

explanation: Great thinking! While regular observation just shows us what is happening, explanatory research digs deeper to find the exact causes.

question: Why is it best to put easy, general questions at the very beginning of a survey?

options.A: To trick the participant into answering difficult items quickly
options.B: To ensure the statistical software can read the demographic data
options.C: To shorten the total amount of time needed for data collection
options.D: To help the participant feel comfortable and build trust

explanation: Starting with gentle, straightforward questions eases anxiety and encourages people to complete the rest of the questionnaire. Brilliant thinking!

question: Which type of stretcher splits into two halves so you can slide it under a patient without rolling them?

options.A: Scoop stretcher
options.B: Basket stretcher
options.C: Canvas folding stretcher
options.D: Rigid spine board

explanation: Spot on! A scoop stretcher splits lengthwise, making it super helpful when you want to avoid rolling a fragile patient.

question: A pregnant patient at 28 weeks complains of severe heartburn after eating. What is the best advice to give her?

options.A: Lie flat on your back immediately after meals to rest your digestion
options.B: Take strong laxatives every evening to empty your bowels completely
options.C: Eat small, frequent meals and avoid lying down right after eating
options.D: Drink large glasses of water with every meal to dilute stomach acid

explanation: Smaller meals keep the stomach from getting overloaded, and staying upright uses gravity to keep the acid where it belongs!

question: A community health nurse conducts a survey to find out why mothers in a village do not bring children for immunization. What is the practical value of this study?

options.A: It guides the creation of a targeted local health education program
options.B: It forces every parent to pay a fine for missed immunizations
options.C: It proves that vaccines cure all known infectious diseases instantly
options.D: It replaces the need to administer vaccines in the clinic

explanation: By finding out the exact reasons for vaccine hesitancy, the nurse can design a friendly, localized outreach program that really helps the community. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h8)

question: Why do nurses need to speak up and do advocacy work alongside regular bedside care?

options.A: Patients will refuse medications unless nurses also lobby local leaders
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to submit weekly political reports
options.C: Clinical care alone cannot fix underlying systemic gaps causing illness
options.D: Clinical nursing duties do not take up enough of a nurse's work shift

explanation: Great thinking! Treating patients at the bedside is vital, but if bad living conditions or broken policies keep making people sick, we have to advocate for wider changes too.

question: Why do voluntary agencies often include counseling in programs for stigmatized illnesses?

options.A: To replace the need for laboratory blood tests
options.B: To help patients cope with emotional distress and social stigma
options.C: To gather evidence for criminal court prosecutions
options.D: To force patients to relocate to urban cities

explanation: You nailed it. Illnesses like HIV or tuberculosis come with heavy emotional weight; counseling gives patients the mental strength to keep taking their treatment.

question: A patient with severe dehydration is expected to show which kidney response regulated by hormones?

options.A: Low levels of ADH leading to dilute, high-volume urine
options.B: Massive secretion of sodium and water into the distal tubule
options.C: High levels of ADH leading to concentrated, low-volume urine
options.D: Complete stoppage of all tubular reabsorption in the cortex

explanation: Dehydration stimulates the release of ADH, causing the kidneys to conserve water and produce small amounts of very concentrated urine. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h8)

question: In the ABCDE emergency assessment, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Coma
options.B: Circulation
options.C: Cardiac
options.D: Comfort

explanation: Well done! In the ABCDE routine, C stands for Circulation. It's all about checking pulses, blood pressure, and stopping any heavy bleeding.

question: What common complication happens when pieces of a heart valve growth break off and travel in the bloodstream?

options.A: Bone fracture
options.B: Kidney stones
options.C: Stroke
options.D: Asthma attack

explanation: When those infected clumps break free, they travel through blood vessels and can block blood flow to the brain, leading to a stroke. Spotting this early saves lives!

question: Why is food safety such a big priority for community health nurses?

options.A: It directly reduces preventable gastrointestinal infections
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for community health clinics
options.C: It is the only way to treat chronic medical conditions
options.D: It stops all forms of malnutrition instantly

explanation: Spot on! When we teach and practice good food safety, we cut down massively on those painful, preventable stomach infections that bring patients into our clinics.

question: What is a major risk of allowing thick frost to build up inside a vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: It turns all the liquid vaccines into solid blocks
options.B: It causes the outside walls to become very hot
options.C: It reduces the cooling efficiency of the appliance
options.D: It creates an unpleasant smell inside the storage unit

explanation: Excess frost acts as an insulation layer that prevents the refrigerator from maintaining its proper internal temperature. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h3)

question: What does a "double burden of disease" mean in Nigerian public health?

options.A: Having high rates of both maternal and child mortality simultaneously
options.B: Suffering from simultaneous outbreaks of waterborne and airborne infections
options.C: Managing high patient loads in both rural clinics and urban teaching hospitals
options.D: Dealing with both infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable diseases

explanation: Great job! A double burden simply means our healthcare system has to fight old enemies like malaria and TB while also managing the rising wave of lifestyle diseases like hypertension and diabetes.

question: How does untreated malnutrition directly affect a patient's recovery in the hospital?

options.A: It causes immediate memory loss in older adults
options.B: It lowers blood pressure to dangerous levels instantly
options.C: It delays wound healing and increases infection risk
options.D: It stops intravenous medications from working entirely

explanation: Without proper nutrients, the body lacks the building blocks needed to repair tissue and fight off hospital germs. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of running biochemical tests on an isolated microbe?

options.A: To see what chemical reactions and nutrients the microbe uses, helping identify the species
options.B: To make the bacteria glow brightly under ordinary room lighting
options.C: To measure how fast liquid broth evaporates in a warm room
options.D: To completely destroy the cell wall so the organism dissolves

explanation: Well done! Biochemical tests check how a germ processes different chemicals, giving scientists a clear chemical fingerprint to identify it.

question: What is the biggest safety risk you must watch out for when using a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Acute kidney failure
options.B: Scalding from hot water or steam
options.C: Sudden systemic drug toxicity
options.D: Permanent hearing loss

explanation: Spot on! Because you are working with boiling water, the main danger is accidental spills causing painful burns to the patient's skin or face.

question: What do we mainly mean by 'sewage' in public health?

options.A: Liquid waste from homes, businesses, and factories
options.B: Treated drinking water stored in community reservoirs
options.C: Industrial runoff containing only chemical fertilizers
options.D: Rainwater collected exclusively from street gutters

explanation: Think of sewage as the used, dirty water flowing away from residential houses, offices, and factories. It carries everyday waste and needs safe management to keep our communities healthy!
